answer_points: A sodium atom loses one electron.
An oxygen atom gains two electrons.
So two sodium atoms react with one oxygen atom.
Na⁺ and O²⁻ ions form, which are sodium ions and oxide ions, with full outer shells.
worked_example.question: Explain what happens to sodium atoms and to oxygen atoms when sodium reacts with oxygen to produce sodium oxide (Na₂O). Answer in terms of electrons.
worked_example.tip: The ratio mark is for two sodium atoms to one oxygen atom. Any one of the final ideas scores the last mark.

key_idea: In ionic bonding, a metal atom transfers outer-shell electrons to a non-metal atom. The metal becomes a positive ion and the non-metal a negative ion. Each ion has a full outer shell, like a noble gas, and the opposite charges attract.

blocks.text: Ionic bonds form when a metal atom reacts with a non-metal atom. This section covers what happens to the electrons and the charge on each ion.

items.meaning: An atom or group of atoms with a positive or negative charge.
A positive ion, made when an atom loses electrons.
A negative ion, made when an atom gains electrons.
The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

items: Metal atoms **lose** electrons from their outer shell and become positive ions.
Non-metal atoms **gain** electrons and become negative ions.
The ions formed by Groups 1, 2, 6 and 7 have the electronic structure of a noble gas, with a full outer shell.
Noble gases (Group 0) do not form ions.

blocks.text: The charge relates to the group number. A Group 3 metal such as gallium loses three electrons to make a 3+ ion, Ga³⁺.

blocks.label: A metal atom forming an ion (Group 1)
A non-metal atom forming an ion (Group 7)

items: Metals lose electrons to make positive ions. Non-metals gain electrons to make negative ions.
Group 1 makes 1+, Group 2 makes 2+, Group 6 makes 2−, Group 7 makes 1−.
The ions have a full outer shell, the same electronic structure as a noble gas.

blocks.text: A dot and cross diagram shows the electron transfer. This section covers how sodium and chlorine form sodium chloride and how to work out the numbers of atoms.

items.text: Draw the outer shell of each atom. Use dots for the metal's electrons and crosses for the non-metal's.
Show the metal's outer electrons moving to the non-metal. Sodium gives one electron to chlorine.
Draw each ion in square brackets with its charge at the top right: [Na]⁺ and [Cl]⁻.
Each ion should have a full outer shell. Chloride has eight electrons, one of them the dot from sodium.

items: The total charge on the compound is zero.
Magnesium loses two electrons and oxygen gains two, so one atom reacts with one atom: Mg²⁺ and O²⁻.
Sodium loses one electron but oxygen needs two, so two sodium atoms react with one oxygen atom: Na₂O.
Calcium loses two electrons but chlorine gains only one, so one calcium atom reacts with two chlorine atoms: CaCl₂.

items: A dot and cross diagram shows electrons moving from the metal to the non-metal.
The number of electrons lost must equal the number gained.
Name the ions as well: sodium ions and chloride ions.

blocks.text: Once the ions have formed, opposite charges attract. This section covers what the ionic bond is and what it is not.

items: An ionic bond is the strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Electrons are transferred, not shared.
It is the ions that attract each other, not the atoms.
In a covalent bond, by contrast, atoms share a pair of electrons.
Ionic bonds hold oppositely charged ions together by electrostatic attraction.
Say "transfer" for ionic bonding and "share" for covalent bonding.
